title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (previous page). K is an abstract topological field isomorphic to C, with no isomorphism chosen. M is a motive over K. Betti realization comes from X(K), and the comparison gives Betti(M)⊗K ≅ DR(M). This puts a real structure (conjugation σ) on DR(M). The Hodge filtration F together with σ yields a canonical bigrading H^{p,q} (F^p ∩ σ(F^q) splitting), so the bigrading needs no choice of isomorphism K ≅ C. Choosing u: K → C additionally gives a C^*-action (Deligne-torus action) on DR(M).

This page, first part. The complex structure induced via u is not intrinsic. Replacing u by its conjugate ū does not simply replace the torus action by its 'symmetric' one. That is, the passage from bigrading to S-action depends on the choice of i or -i. Marginal addition: for the conjugate motive M_σ (base change of M along the nontrivial automorphism of K), composing the σ-semilinear de Rham identification with σ gives a K-linear isomorphism DR(M_σ) ≅ DR(M). It preserves the Q-(Betti) structures and exchanges each filtration with its opposite.

Second part: motives over K_0 = R. Let K be an algebraic closure of R. DR(M)_K = DR(M_K) carries two real structures:
- τ, from descent of de Rham cohomology to R (τ respects the Hodge filtration);
- σ, the Betti/complex conjugation from above (σ does not respect the filtration).
Both are antilinear. Claim: σ and τ commute, i.e. DR(M_K)^σ ≅ H^*(X(K), R) is τ-stable. Reason: τ restricted to Betti cohomology is induced (up to the coefficient conjugation) by the antiholomorphic involution τ_X of X(K). Hence στ = τσ = f_R is a K-linear involution of H^*(X(K), K). It is the map induced by τ_X, i.e. the real Frobenius F_∞, which is rational on H^*(X(K), Q).

Next page: a motive over R gives a Hodge structure V plus a rational involution F_∞ exchanging F with its opposite. In the motivic Galois group G this gives F_∞ ∈ G(Q), of order 2, generating G/G^0 and normalizing h: S → G_R via the canonical symmetry of S. This is exactly the data later formalized as real Hodge structures with F_∞ (Deligne's 'Valeurs de fonctions L', 1979).
errors: σ and τ are both antilinear. The struck-out word 'antilinéaires' was correct, and only their product f_R is K-linear.

The remark about replacing u(λ) by its conjugate is stated tersely and without proof. The precise statement is that changing u to ū exchanges the roles of z and z̄ in z^{-p} z̄^{-q}; it is plausible but not checked on the page.
'σ ne respecte pas la filtration' is right in general. It would respect F only if the Hodge structure were concentrated in a single bidegree.

ideas.what: Hodge bigrading defined intrinsically for an abstract field K ≅ C without choosing the isomorphism; only the torus action depends on the choice of i
ideas.modern_name: Hodge structures over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 complete for an archimedean absolute value; dependence of h: S→G on choice of √-1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Théorie de Hodge II, 1971; Hodge cycles 1982)

ideas.what: Conjugate motive M_σ with a K-linear isomorphism DR(M_σ) ≅ DR(M) preserving Q-structures and reversing filtrations
ideas.modern_name: Conjugate varieties / conjugate Hodge structure; de Rham descent along complex conjugation

ideas.what: For motives over R: two commuting real structures on DR(M_C) (Betti σ, de Rham descent τ) whose product is the involution induced by complex conjugation on X(C)
ideas.modern_name: Real Frobenius F_∞; comparison F_∞ ∘ c_B = c_DR
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne, 'Valeurs de fonctions L et périodes d'intégrales' (1979)

missed.claim: Grothendieck had, around 1970, the real Frobenius F_∞ as the product of Betti and de Rham conjugations on a motive over R. On the next page it becomes an element of the motivic Galois group normalizing the Deligne torus. This predates Deligne's 1979 formalization, though it is consistent with it and likely transmitted orally.
missed.quote: Alors σ et τ commutent ... Alors στ = τσ = f_R est l'automorphisme de H^*(X(K),K)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority and attribution only; mathematically fully absorbed in the literature on Deligne's period conjecture and motives over R.

deep.surprise_reason: Correct, careful set-up of the real Frobenius and of Hodge structures for motives over R. All of it is now standard (Deligne 1979, Deligne–Milne), so the page is of historical interest only as an early Grothendieck version.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 likely reads 'pour la bigraduation définie par ...' rather than 'pour la conjugaison définie par Hodge'. The bigrading is intrinsic; the complex (torus) structure is not.
Marginal insertion: '(C le complété)' is doubtful. It more plausibly reads 'le motif M_σ (σ l'aut. ... de K)' or similar, referring to the conjugate motive.
'les structures entrelacées[?]' is better read as 'les structures rationnelles/vectorielles'. The conclusion 'conservant les Q-structures et renversant filtrations' supports this.
'σ et τ sont [-antilinéaires-]': the struck word is antilinéaires and the line continues; the underlined word may be a replacement.
